items.title: Bell says cybersecurity incident affected customers at Virgin Plus, Lucky Mobile
items.summary_auto: A spokesperson for Bell says customers across its network of subsidiaries, including Virgin Plus and Lucky Mobile, were affected by a Nov. 17 breach but no "highly sensitive" information such as credit card numbers or banking information was impacted.

items.title: Sold! Why live cattle auctions still matter to Alberta ranchers in an era of online bidding
items.summary_auto: Ranchers say you can still tell when it’s auction day in farming towns: trucks are lined up on the streets, the coffee shops are busy and local commerce surges.

items.title: Canadians fed up with long hold times want telcos to answer calls within 10 minutes
Who's spying on whom and why?
items.summary_auto: NVIDIA's former CEO is alleged to have been compromised by a Chinese spy. We explore the state of spycraft in the contemporary age.

items.title: Spying on survivors: Why RCMP watched Wab Kinew's father in the 1960s
items.summary_auto: Manitoba Premier Wab Kinew wants to know who spied on his father for the RCMP, and why. Documents obtained by CBC News reveal the late Anishinaabe leader Tobasonakwut Kinew was under surveillance in the 1960s, an early target in a countrywide infiltration initiative later dubbed the "Native extremism program."

items.title: Audience evacuated from Don Toliver concert in Manchester after unknown substance released in crowd
items.summary_auto: More than 12,000 fans were evacuated from a concert by American rapper Don Toliver after an unknown substance was released in the crowd, British police said Monday.

items.title: A gold mine has created a 'little town' in central Newfoundland — and it's about to get bigger
items.summary_auto: Step inside the Valentine gold mine near Buchans, which is now Atlantic Canada's largest.

items.title: N.L. fisheries minister stayed in Scottish castle, ‘luxury’ shooting lodge on aquaculture giant’s dime
items.summary_auto: Newfoundland and Labrador’s NDP says the province’s fisheries minister put himself in a “brutal” conflict of interest when he stayed in a castle, then a “luxury” shooting lodge — all on the dime of an aquaculture company — during a trip to Scotland last June.

items.title: Inside India's bold plan to transform its largest slum, Dharavi, into a multibillion-dollar development
items.summary_auto: India's largest slum is being cleared to make room for a modern urban development to include rehabilitated slum housing plus luxury condos and office towers. It's a massive regeneration project, funded by private and public money. But will it work?

items.title: More Canadians are using cannabis daily than are drinking alcohol daily: study
items.summary_auto: Daily use of cannabis has outstripped daily use of alcohol in Canada, with young Canadians at the front of the trend, new data shows. Experts say this generational shift brings some positives, but that many Canadians remain unaware that there are risks with overuse of cannabis.

items.title: Feds launch recruitment for independent Miscarriage of Justice Review Commission
items.summary_auto: Guilt or innocence will not be determined by the commission, but it will instead investigate potential miscarriage of justice and may order a remedy, such as a new trial or new appeal.

items.title: Big tech, law enforcement make final pitches as Senate considers data access bill's future
items.summary_auto: Big tech is launching its final salvo to scale back the Liberal government's contentious proposed national security legislation, which would change how companies retain and hand over user data to Canadian police and intelligence officers, as it nears its last legislative hurdle in the Senate. Law enforcement agencies are also making a passionate appeal for senators to pass the bill as soon as possible.

items.title: Toronto to receive $29M top-up for crossing guards that speed cameras used to fund
items.summary_auto: The Ford government banned speed cameras across Ontario in November 2025, leaving many cities worrying about safety and funding. Now, the City of Toronto looks set to receive a one-time payment of almost $30 million to help with lost revenue that used to pay for crossing guards.

items.title: 'Unprecedented': Why this round of Stellantis, Unifor contract talks is like no other
items.summary_auto: In the spring, Unifor Local 444 president James Stewart, who represents 6,000 workers at the Stellantis assembly plant in Windsor, Ont., warned that this year's contract talks with the global carmaker would be the toughest round of bargaining ever in the powerful union's long history — even worse than during the 2008 financial crisis. He seems to have been right.

items.title: Carney, opposition leaders trade comedic jabs at press gallery dinner
Closure of longtime Vancouver burger chain highlights growing pressures on B.C. restaurants
items.summary_auto: After 16 years in business, a Vancouver burger chain has announced the permanent closure of its restaurants because of ongoing financial challenges. It's the latest in a series of closures highlighting the pressures facing the food service industry.

items.title: Montreal Canadiens acquire centre Dylan Larkin from Red Wings in blockbuster trade
items.summary_auto: The Red Wings traded centre Dylan Larkin to the Montreal Canadiens in a blockbuster deal on Sunday, ending a drawn-out saga after Detroit's former captain requested a move in the off-season.

items.title: First Nations leader warns of 'dire' consequences if B.C. repeals the Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act
items.summary_auto: British Columbia's new Conservative government could face "dire" consequences if they repeal the Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act as promised, a First Nations leader said, adding that he's willing to work with new Premier Lorne Doerkson.

items.title: COP31 climate talks collapse after member states reject deal for not mentioning fossil fuels
Pay halted for suspended Vancouver police officer charged with fraud and theft
items.summary_auto: The Vancouver Police Board has discontinued pay for a high-profile officer accused of fraud and theft.

items.title: UN-affiliated athlete swims in dangerous Strait of Hormuz to highlight Iran war's impact on wildlife
items.summary_auto: Lewis Pugh, who is a United Nations Patron of the Oceans, spent three days last week swimming parts of the dangerous waterway to highlight how Iran war threatens the area's habitat and wildlife.

items.title: Trump calling Putin a friend is 'appalling,' says former ambassador to NATO
items.summary_auto: Kurt Volker, former U.S. Ambassador to NATO, tells CBC's Rosemary Barton that it’s 'appalling' to hear U.S. President Donald Trump double down on calling Russian President Vladimir Putin his 'friend.' Volker also weighs in on the leaked classified Pentagon memo about restricting defence ties with Canada.

items.title: A small latte and a chat, please: Why this B.C. café owner put conversation on the menu
items.summary_auto: Registered clinical counsellor Shane Trudell estimates one-third of the population suffers from loneliness — but many people aren't aware of it. A New Westminster café hopes to help.

items.title: Miley Cyrus weds Maxx Morando in California, People magazine reports
items.summary_auto: Grammy-winning pop star Miley Cyrus married her longtime partner, drummer Maxx ‌Morando, in California on Saturday, People magazine and other U.S. entertainment news ​outlets reported.
